description:
FOUND s509 (Fable, 2026-10-06) by the review probes for s507c PART TWO; PRE-EXISTING on main fee16466, unchanged by that batch.

REPRODUCER (~/pcl-agent-scratch/s509/review/misc/sl.pl; perl 5.40.3 vs main):
  sub g  { (@_)[0, 1] }         my $s7 = g(7, 8, 9);      perl: 8    PCL: 2
  sub h2 { return (@_)[1, 2] }  my $s8 = h2(7, 8, 9);     perl: 9    PCL: 2
RIGHT TODAY (same file): a list slice assigned to a scalar directly -- `my $s = (7, 8, 9)[0, 1]`, `(@a)[0, 1]`, `@a[0, 1]`,
`(sort @a)[-1, 0]`, `(f())[1, 2]`, `(split /,/, "a,b,c")[0, 2]` -- and an ARRAY slice as the last statement
(`sub k { my @x = @_; @x[0, 1] }` gives 8).  So the slice's own scalar rule (its last element) is implemented; what is
missing is the route by which a sub's RETURN VALUE takes its context from the caller for a parenthesised LIST slice: the
slice is built as a list and the caller's scalar context then counts it, as it would an array.

RELATED: #2004 (completed) fixed the scalar context LEAKING INTO `return (LIST)[i]`; this is the opposite direction for a
multi-index slice -- the caller's scalar context must REACH it.

CHEAP DISCRIMINATING MEASUREMENT (not taken): `./pl2cl` on the two-line reproducer and on `sub k` -- compare what wraps
the slice in the return position (the array-slice spelling is the working sibling: rule 11, route the list slice through
the same context-aware return form).

PRIORITY: low-medium (silent wrong; `return (stat $f)[7, 9]` / `(localtime)[5, 4]` returned from a helper and used in
scalar context is the realistic spelling).
subject: SILENT WRONG: a LIST SLICE that is a sub's return value gives its element COUNT when the sub is called in scalar context -- `sub g { (@_)[0, 1] } my $s = g(7, 8, 9)` is 2 in PCL, 8 in perl (the slice's last element); the same for `return (@_)[1, 2]`
